name: トラットリア ディベルテンテ (Trattoria DiverTente)

claims.text: No information available on cross-contamination controls. Active pizza and pasta production means wheat flour is in continuous use throughout the kitchen.

Italian cuisine focus means soy sauce is unlikely in main dishes, but no explicit confirmation that wheat-based soy sauce is absent from all preparations. Confirm with staff for any dish that may use Japanese-inflected seasoning (e.g., the Shinshu miso pizza).
Dairy (cream cheese, quiche) and meat (venison, pork) are core menu components; no segregated vegan prep surfaces are mentioned.
No allergy-handling policy or trained allergy protocol has been described in any source reviewed. Phone reservation (026-466-6650) is the recommended channel to discuss dietary needs before visiting.
Strong seasonal, locally sourced produce ethos — the owner explicitly shapes menus around available vegetables, which may allow for ad-hoc vegetable-forward dishes when asked.
Oyaki dough is wheat-flour based by recipe — this is not a cross-contamination risk but a fundamental ingredient issue. The product is not suitable for anyone avoiding gluten.

Soy sauce is used in oyaki fillings (confirmed in general oyaki ingredient descriptions for similar Nagano shops); standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

No allergen segregation information is available. Multiple fillings are prepared in the same shop including dairy-containing (cheese) and fish-based seasonings. Cross-contact between fillings cannot be excluded.

No allergen menu, allergy handling protocol, or dietary labeling is listed on the shop's website or any review source. Staff interaction is minimal at this walk-up counter format. Diners with serious allergies should contact the shop directly before visiting.

Vegetable-filled oyaki varieties (nozawana, eggplant, kabocha, mushroom) are plant-based in their primary filling ingredients, which may suit some dietary preferences — but full ingredient disclosure is not publicly available.
No information found about dedicated fryers or GF cross-contamination protocols. Kitchen setup is unknown.
Soy sauce usage in curries or marinades is not documented in any source reviewed. Wheat content of curry bases is unconfirmed — standard Japanese curry roux typically contains wheat.
No dedicated vegan preparation area is noted. The kitchen handles meat-based curries (beef, butter chicken, shrimp) alongside any plant-based options, so cross-contact is likely.

The Nagano City official tourism listing notes 'アレルギー対応' (allergy accommodation) as an available service, suggesting staff will engage with allergy questions. Direct inquiry at the counter is advised.
Staff confirmed they can remove shrimp from the green curry upon request, showing some willingness to modify dishes for dietary needs.

name: 明日のためのしじみばか 泉店 (Ashita no Tame no Shijimibaka Izumi-ten)

claims.text: No dedicated GF preparation area or fryer documented. Standard izakaya kitchen — cross-contamination from wheat via soy sauce, marinades, and shared cooking surfaces must be assumed.

Shijimi dashi broth is the restaurant's specialty, but conventional wheat-containing soy sauce (醤油) is standard in Japanese oden broth and yakitori marinades. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative was documented anywhere.
Shijimi (clam) dashi is the foundational stock used across virtually all dishes. Oysters are a featured menu item. No plant-only cooking zone exists.
No allergy menu, allergy questionnaire, or staff training documentation was found in any source. Guests with serious food allergies should call ahead (052-228-3531) before visiting.

The core broth is made from shijimi (freshwater clams), not from wheat-containing or fermented products — so the broth base itself may be inherently wheat-light, though the soy sauce used to season it almost certainly contains wheat unless tamari is specifically requested.
No fryer information is documented. The kitchen handles marinated meats and offal; cross-contamination risk from shared equipment is unknown.

No allergen menu exists. Standard Japanese soy sauce containing wheat is the expected baseline for yakiniku tare and marinades at this type of establishment — no wheat-free soy sauce or tamari is mentioned anywhere.
This is an all-meat establishment; every surface and grill is in contact with animal products. No plant-based preparation area exists.
No allergy-handling protocol has been documented for this restaurant. Phone reservations are accepted and calling ahead (052-551-0598) in Japanese is the only known channel for allergy enquiries.

name: シャンブル ダンファン (Chambre d'enfants)

claims.text: No information published on whether soy sauce used in sauces or glazes contains wheat. Standard in Japanese French kitchens to use conventional wheat-bearing soy sauce.
Every documented dish contains animal products. No plant-based courses exist. Cross-contact with animal fats, stocks, and proteins throughout the kitchen is near-certain.

No allergy or dietary restriction handling policy is published on any platform. The reservation-only format (phone: 052-990-4513) theoretically allows guests to raise dietary needs at booking, but no accommodation has been confirmed by any source.
うどん・きしめん・中華そば等の小麦麺と同一の調理環境（茹で釜など）でそばを提供している可能性が高く、グルテン交差汚染のリスクがあります。
つゆ・だしに使用される醤油は一般的に小麦を含みます。アレルギー対応醤油の使用は確認されていません。
全メニューのだしが動物性（かつお・煮干し等）ベースと考えられ、植物性食材のみの料理でも同一設備での調理による接触が生じます。
アレルギー対応・グルテンフリー対応についての情報は一切公表されていません。来店前に電話（052-531-5130）で直接確認することを強く推奨します。
Standard Japanese shoyu (wheat-containing soy sauce) is used in ramen broths at this type of shop; no tamari or wheat-free alternative is mentioned in any source.
